map.state: SOFI 2026 nowcasts 645 million people undernourished in 2025 (7.8%, range 608–696 million), about 14 million fewer than in 2024. Separately, 266 million people in 47 food-crisis countries and territories faced high acute food insecurity in 2025, 22.9% of those analysed.
map.compared_with: 658.8 million (8.1%) in 2024 (SOFI 2026, Tables 2.1 and 2.2, same revised series). 2025 is a nowcast, and SOFI says it may not fully reflect the worsening situation in humanitarian crises. The acute figure has no like comparison: 296 million in 53 countries in 2024, and the GRFC says the fall mainly reflects fewer countries covered. Its analysed share was 22.7% in 2024. Mid-year Update, data to 31 August 2026: of 33 comparable countries and territories 17 improved, 15 worsened.

map.state: World Inequality Lab estimates, 2025: the global top 10% took 53% of income and held 75% of wealth, the bottom half 8% and 2%. The top 0.001% held nearly 6.1% of wealth, up from around 3.8% in 1995. Average income in North America & Oceania is about 13 times Sub-Saharan Africa's.
map.compared_with: Top 0.001% held around 3.8% of wealth in 1995 (World Inequality Report 2026, Figure 2, same series). The bottom half's share has stagnated at around 2% since the early 2000s. Income points the other way since 2000: top 10% 58% to 53%, bottom half 7% to 8% (Figure 1.9), and the report finds little long-term change since 1910.

map.state: September 2026 was 1.63°C above pre-industrial and the 12 months to it 1.50°C; the month was the second-warmest September in Copernicus's ERA5 record. EM-DAT recorded 358 natural-hazard disasters, 16,607 deaths and 110.2 million people affected in 2025, figures still evolving.
map.compared_with: 1.47°C in September 2025 (same ERA5 series and baseline). January to September 2026 ranks above the same months of 2023 and 2025, below 2024. EM-DAT's 2025 deaths and people affected lie below its 2005–2024 averages of 57,429 and 169.0 million, but it cites reporting delays and no mega-disaster, and calls the burden typical.

map.state: UN IGME estimates 4.9 million children died before age five in 2024, down from 6.1 million in 2015, and the pace of decline has slowed by 61%. DR Congo's Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak reached 10,414 confirmed cases, including 5,372 deaths, by 30 October 2026 (INSP).
map.compared_with: 6,096,000 under-five deaths in 2015 and 42.9 per 1,000 live births, against 4,858,000 and 37.4 in 2024 (UN IGME report 2025, Tables 1 and 4). The annual rate of reduction fell from 3.9% in 2000–2015 to 1.5% in 2015–2024. Ebola points the other way: 9,704 confirmed cases, including 4,687 deaths, on 20 October 2026 (INSP SitRep N°159); part of the rise in deaths since is Ituri's data harmonisation of 29 October.

map.state: UNHCR estimates 117.8 million people were forcibly displaced at end-2025, 5.4 million fewer than a year earlier, with many returns under adverse circumstances. OCHA's plans list 252.8 million people in need in 2026; its global appeal was 44.3% funded on 1 November.
map.compared_with: About 123.2 million at end-2024, 5.4 million more (UNHCR Global Trends 2025, same count). UNHCR estimated about 117 to 118 million at end-April 2026. Funding on 1 November 2026: US$15.54bn of US$35.06bn (OCHA FTS).
